_doc: Corpus-completeness manifest (Arc 1 S4). One row per conformance-corpus
family: every test_fixtures/ subdirectory plus every workspace/tests/
entry. scripts/check_corpus_manifest.py enforces it in CI (the
workspace-json-fresh lane): required consumers present, active-port
symmetry where declared, no unknown families, no orphaned fixtures.
kind: source = hand-authored inputs; compiled = generated from a source
corpus or a canonical generator; fixtures = driver cases + pinned
goldens. required_consumers is the BLOCKING set (POLICY.md #1: active
ports rust+swift, the reference interpreter, and the scripts/ gates;
the frozen OCaml/Python-Qt ports run at the five-port-parity tag and
are deliberately untracked here). port_symmetry: the rust and swift
claimed sets (after the transitive data-reference closure) must be
identical for the family. claim_style is documentation of HOW each
consumer registers fixtures — the checker's extraction rules implement
TWO gap lists, of opposite shapes: known_gaps SUPPRESSES a named
mechanical check (and a row that suppresses nothing is reported stale);
coverage_gaps DECLARES what the corpus cannot reach at all and is
printed on every run. See _coverage_gaps_doc at the foot of this file.

test_fixtures/properties.notes: PROPERTY corpus, and the first family of its kind here -- it is NOT a golden set. Per the ruled doctrine ('the checker is the law; the corpus is its witnesses; the generative lane is its growing confidence') each file carries WITNESSES for a predicate rather than expected outputs. shift_constrain_square.json holds 11 hand-searched vectors per tool for the Shift-constrain invariant (rx == ry / width == height, BIT-EXACT, at any zoom and pan); the checker also runs 384 FRESH vectors per run from a nanosecond seed, replayable via JAS_PROPERTY_SEED. Two witnesses are deliberately NON-discriminating and labelled so -- they are the shape of the hand smoke test that passed while DYADICSIDE was broken at every zoom but 100%. Both runners carry a `dyadicside_mutant` reproducing the pre-fix arithmetic and assert every witness's `discriminating` flag against it each run, and the generative lane REFUSES a run in which fewer than 20 of 384 fresh vectors could catch that bug -- so this corpus cannot decay into asserting nothing, which is the failure mode that looks exactly like success.

_coverage_gaps_doc: The SECOND gap list, and the opposite shape from known_gaps above.
known_gaps is a suppressor: each row names one mechanical check on one
family/file and downgrades its failure to a warning, so it can only
ever speak about a check this gate already runs. coverage_gaps records
what the gate does NOT check -- a family whose fixtures never reach the
interesting branch, a field no fixture sets, a divergence no
port-vs-port comparison can see. It suppresses nothing; every row is
printed on every run, precisely so a green gate stops implying a
completeness it never had.
Required keys: id, title, evidence, blocks, unblock (census optional).
`evidence` must be a claim someone can re-run, because a gap you cannot
state precisely is not ready to record. Every row below was re-measured
on this commit rather than copied from the census -- three census
figures did not survive that (noted in the rows), and the census's
hit_test/marquee row is not here at all because it has since CLOSED:
element_intersects_rect and element_intersects_polygon are now driven
by both roundtrip binaries over 6 of hit_test.json's 40 vectors.
Census rows 5.3, 5.6, 5.10 and 5.11 are deliberately absent: they are
real, but this pass did not re-verify them, and an unverified row here
would be the same false assurance the empty list was.

coverage_gaps.title: scripts/check_encoding_hygiene.py cannot see subprocess text pipes, so 17 sites — including all twelve invocations inside the three BLOCKING cross-language drivers — still decode child-process stdout with the locale codec rather than UTF-8
coverage_gaps.evidence: Re-measured on this commit, not copied. `grep -rnE 'text\s*=\s*True|universal_newlines\s*=\s*True|check_output\(|\.decode\(\s*\)' --include=*.py workspace_interpreter scripts jas_flask` returns 20 lines, of which 2 are check_encoding_hygiene.py:62-63 — the gate's own DOCSTRING describing this gap, which matches the grep for it. The real count is 17 call sites, every one `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, text=True)`: cross_language_algorithms.py:144,155,166,177; cross_language_commutativity.py:76,87,98,109; cross_language_workspace.py:53,68,79,90; ingest_recording.py:182,421; check_naming_rule.py:205; check_corpus_manifest.py:993; gui_probe_swift.py:198. `text=True` decodes with `locale.getpreferredencoding(False)`, measured cp1252 on the Windows box that found this class, NOT UTF-8. The gate walks the AST for builtin open() and pathlib read_text/write_text only, so none of the 17 is reachable by it. WHETHER ANY OF THEM CURRENTLY CARRIES NON-ASCII IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and the one probe run argues against it: 28 files under test_fixtures/{algorithms,expected,operations} contain raw non-ASCII bytes, but invoking the driver's own binary as the driver does — `jas_dioxus/target/debug/algorithm_roundtrip.exe align test_fixtures/algorithms/align.json` — returned 1051 bytes with ZERO bytes above 0x7F and no \u escapes, so that fixture's non-ASCII lives in doc fields the binary does not echo. This row records a STRUCTURAL hole with a demonstrated mechanism and an UNDEMONSTRATED exposure; it is not evidence that the drivers are currently wrong.
coverage_gaps.blocks: Nothing today, on the evidence above. What it blocks is the CLAIM: a green check_encoding_hygiene.py reads as 'this repository decodes text explicitly', and that sentence is false for 17 sites, twelve of which sit in the blocking cross-language equivalence lane. If a port ever emits a raw non-ASCII byte on stdout — an element `name`, a text run, a path string, a panic message — the three drivers would mojibake or raise UnicodeDecodeError on Windows and be correct everywhere else, which is precisely the shape of defect that took a first Windows run to find at all. The frozen ports' 43 encoding and 7 newline sites are excluded by policy and are NOT part of this gap.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Two routes. (a) Mechanical, and cheap: pass `encoding='utf-8'` alongside `text=True` at all 17 sites, then extend the gate's AST walk to flag `subprocess.run`/`Popen`/`check_output` carrying `text=True` or `universal_newlines=True` without an explicit `encoding=`, with a self-test class proving it goes RED — at which point this row is deleted rather than amended. The gate's docstring must be exempted from its own grep, per the self-reference above. (b) Evidential, and the reason (a) was not simply done: establish first whether any port binary can emit raw non-ASCII on stdout at all. If every payload is ASCII-safe JSON by construction, the honest fix is to PIN that property with a test rather than to add an encoding argument that no input can exercise — an unexercised fix reads as protection and is not.
coverage_gaps.census: 17 sites, measured 2026-07-28 on the first Windows run of this project's gates; the same run fixed 91 encoding and 37 newline sites that the gate CAN see.

coverage_gaps.title: The preservation gate can only reach violations expressible in op_apply's verb vocabulary, so six of EDIT_SEMANTICS_FREEZE.md §3.5's rows stay invisible to it
coverage_gaps.evidence: Measured on this commit by grepping the dispatchers. op_apply has exactly ONE boolean verb in each port (jas_dioxus/src/document/op_apply.rs `"boolean_union"`, JasSwift/Sources/Document/OpApply.swift `case "boolean_union"`) and ZERO verbs matching apply_mask / set_width_points / make_compound_shape / boolean_subtract / boolean_intersect / boolean_divide. No verb can produce a PARTIAL (control-point) selection either: the string `Partial` occurs once in the whole of op_apply.rs, inside a `#[derive(...)]`. Consequently these §3.5 rows are unreachable from this corpus: Swift `withMask` .path arm; Swift `withWidthPoints` .path arm; Rust `move_control_points` Rect->Polygon arm (needs a corner drag, i.e. a partial selection); Rust `make_compound_shape_with_op` duplicate id; the boolean SURVIVOR arms (subtract_front / subtract_back / crop / trim / divide) and their Swift `locked: false` + dropped name/id/toolOrigin/mask; and both blob-brush `fillRule` arms (a gesture, not an op). RE-MEASURED 2026-07-27, after the DIVIDE and MERGE arms were repaired in Rust: still exactly ONE boolean verb per port (grep -c for boolean_divide / boolean_merge / boolean_trim over jas_dioxus/src/document/op_apply.rs and JasSwift/Sources/Document/OpApply.swift returns 0 in BOTH files), so neither repaired arm is expressible as a shared vector. JasSwift's applyDestructiveBoolean does implement `case "divide"` and `case "trim", "merge"`, so the missing piece is the op-verb registration, not the arm.
coverage_gaps.blocks: Of the §3.5 table, this gate today catches the Rust UNION frontmost-id carry, the Swift withChildren class (5 vectors), and one of the 41 Swift inline Layer(/Group( literals. The rest of the table is not gated by anything cross-language. Named consequence as of 2026-07-27: the Rust DIVIDE arm (which handed every output region the designated operand's whole `common`, leaving two live elements wearing one id) and the Rust MERGE arm (which elected the frontmost contributor's whole `common` by z-order) were both repaired with per-port batteries in jas_dioxus/src/document/controller.rs's `preservation_law_tests`, and NEITHER repair is visible to any cross-language gate. The Swift twins of both arms are unaudited by this corpus for the same reason.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Two independent routes, both fixture-plus-verb: (a) widen the op vocabulary with the missing boolean verbs and a mask/width-points setter, then add preservation vectors for the 1->1 survivor arms — where subject_fields_only is exactly the right predicate; (b) give the GESTURE corpus the same invariant gate, which reaches the blob-brush arms and the Rect corner drag that the op corpus cannot address. Route (a) is now the cheap one for these two arms specifically: registering `boolean_divide` and `boolean_merge` in both ports' op_apply dispatchers is additive (each delegates to an applyDestructiveBoolean arm that already exists in both), after which a divide vector over preservation_nested_attrs.svg pins id_uniqueness and fresh_ids directly. Expect the swift lane to need pins on that vector until JasSwift's boolean rebuild is brought to the same rule.

coverage_gaps.title: The six preservation invariants say nothing about the FIELDS of a freshly minted element, so the boolean result's lossy kind demotion and its dropped non-paint fields are invisible
coverage_gaps.evidence: The invariants are id_uniqueness / id_survival / consumed_ids_die / fresh_ids / bystanders_unchanged / subject_fields_only. Every one of them is keyed on an id that existed BEFORE the edit; a minted element has no before-image to diff against, so nothing in the set constrains it. Concretely, on the boolean_union_merges_two_rects vector both ports emit a single-ring `Polygon` — the §3.5 row 'Boolean flatten, single-ring arm, both ports' calls that a lossy demotion (a Polygon has no slot for widthPoints / strokeBrush / strokeBrushOverrides / fillRule) — and the gate reports nothing, because the invariants never look at the output's kind or its non-identity fields.
coverage_gaps.blocks: §3.3's unanimity carry, §3.6's per-op paint column, and T1's representation term (no lossy demotion) are all statements ABOUT the minted element. None of them is gated here.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Add a seventh declarative invariant to the vector shape — an `expected_output` block naming the required kind and the fields the result must carry (unanimous values, RESULT_FILL_RULE) — and implement it in both port gates. This is additive to the existing five vectors and needs no new op verbs.

coverage_gaps.title: Swift indexes text by grapheme cluster; Rust and the reference index by Unicode scalar, so no non-ASCII vector can be added to the three text families
coverage_gaps.evidence: Measured through the roundtrip harnesses at char_width 10 on this commit. content "ae\u0301b" (4 scalars / 3 clusters): reference and Rust give char_count 4 with 4 glyphs, Swift gives 3 with 3. The ZWJ family emoji U+1F468 U+200D U+1F469 U+200D U+1F467 (5 scalars / 1 cluster): reference and Rust give 5, Swift gives 1. Total line advance now AGREES (40 and 50 both ports) because the injected measurer counts scalars; it is the per-glyph subdivision and every index derived from it that diverge. Root cause is `Array(content)` in TextLayout.swift and PathTextLayout.swift. (TextLayoutParagraph.swift was cited here in error: it contains ZERO `Array(` occurrences - it holds only the hyphenation/segment/counter helpers.)
coverage_gaps.blocks: text_layout, text_layout_paragraph and path_text_layout are ASCII-only families. The rust-vs-swift comparison has no oracle-holdout mechanism (only property_planar and exact_boolean get one), so a non-ASCII vector cannot be added and marked -- it would simply red the gate.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Move Swift's three layout files onto scalar indices, in the SAME sweep as TextEditSession/TypeTool/TypeOnPathTool, which do their cursor arithmetic in `Character` counts (`text.count`, `key.count == 1`) and would otherwise desync from the layout for exactly these strings.
coverage_gaps.census: 5.9(a), extended: the census called this a harness bug only. The harness half is fixed (HARNESSUNIT); this is the product half it was hiding.

coverage_gaps.title: element_bounds gates a function that ignores transform entirely -- now PINNED as such; the transform-aware bbox is gated by its own family, but still only for a single-layer path
coverage_gaps.evidence: Element::bounds / Element.bounds IGNORE common.transform in both ports -- measured through the two roundtrip binaries, a 10x10 rect at the origin carrying translate(100,50) reports [0,0,10,10] from Rust and from Swift alike. The transform-aware function is element_evaluated_bbox / elementEvaluatedBBox, driven by the element_evaluated_bounds family, now 17 vectors: the original 9 (all RECTS -- translate, non-uniform scale, rotate 45, skewX, a full composed matrix, an ancestor-only layer transform, an element-then-layer composition-order vector, a stroked geometric-vs-preview vector, and a no-transform control) plus 8 NON-RECT ones added the same day (rotated ellipse, cubic under the composed matrix, arc under a layer rotation, scaled group, each with a null-transform control). coverage_gaps.title: Rust's f64::to_radians() and Swift's `deg * .pi / 180` group differently and disagree by an ulp on a QUARTER of all integer degrees; since MATRIXPRECISION the difference reaches the saved SVG bytes
coverage_gaps.evidence: MEASURED through the new transform_apply family over 721 integer degrees: rotate_matrix produced a BIT-DIFFERENT matrix on 184 of them and shear_matrix on 170 of 721 quarter-degree angles, worst absolute difference 4.66e-10 (tan amplifies near the dialog's +/-89.9 clamp). Rust's to_radians is `self * (PI/180.0)`; Swift wrote `angleDeg * .pi / 180`, i.e. `(deg * PI) / 180`. jas_dioxus has 14 to_radians() call sites; JasSwift has 19 `* .pi / 180` sites. TWO of them -- Transform.rotate in Geometry/Element.swift and TransformApply.shearMatrix -- are FIXED (parenthesised to match Rust), which took the sweep from 354 bit-mismatches to 0 with all 2957 Swift tests still green. The other 17 Swift sites are unchanged.
coverage_gaps.blocks: geometry/svg.rs writes matrix entries a/b/c/d at FULL shortest-round-trip precision (MATRIXPRECISION, ruled 2026-07-31), so any unfixed site that reaches a serialized matrix makes the two ports emit different bytes for the same user action -- and every algorithm family's tolerance is 1e-4 or wider, four to six orders above the difference, so no existing family can see it.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Sweep the remaining 17 Swift sites to `deg * (Double.pi / 180)` and add a lint (or a naming-rule row) that refuses the unparenthesised spelling, OR rule that only matrix-serializing sites must agree and name the rest as exempt. Deciding which is a scope call, not a checker-author call.

coverage_gaps.title: offset_path is the one Phase-3 family that CANNOT get a roundtrip verb without a refactor: in Rust it is `#[cfg(feature = "web")]` and takes a web_sys CanvasRenderingContext2d, so the native harness binary cannot even link it
coverage_gaps.evidence: jas_dioxus/src/algorithms/mod.rs line 29 gates the module on the `web` feature, and every entry point takes `&CanvasRenderingContext2d` and draws directly into it -- there is no value returned. The Swift twin is not in Sources/Algorithms at all; it is JasSwift/Sources/Canvas/OffsetPath.swift and takes a CGContext. The extractable geometry (samplePathWithNormals, evaluateWidthAt, the left/right offset rails, and the cap construction) is textually identical in the two ports, but the CAPS are emitted as ctx.arc_with_anticlockwise / CGMutablePath.addArc and never exist as points.

Reading the two, the parameter-space sweeps agree (both spell the decreasing-angle direction) and a nonzero fill is invariant under the y-flip anyway, so the flagged divergence is PROBABLY absent -- but 'probably, from reading' is exactly what this programme exists to replace.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Extract the pure half into a returned outline (a point list plus the cap arcs as sampled points), leaving the two renderers as thin callers. That is a real refactor in both ports and it is the reason this family is declared rather than done.
